top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: A comprehensive literature search yielded a total of 208 articles (Figure 2) relevant to the investigation of interest. Following exclusion based on abstract screening, 16 articles underwent comprehensive full-text review. Ultimately, 13 articles met the prede fi ned inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis, collectively encompassing a cohort of 288 patients. 6,15 -26 12 studies were retrospective, while one study was prospective observational study. Only one study 16 provided data on conventional open surgery as a comparative group, while the other studies exclusively focused on the patients who underwent TEVAR (single group).

top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The selection of articles adhered to stringent inclusion criteria, encompassing original studies reporting the short-term or long-term outcomes of the use of TEVAR for RTAAD or RTAIMH. Exclusion criteria included review articles, case reports, and investigations involving animal subjects. Additionally, studies not documented in the English language were excluded from consideration.

top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The initial screening of articles was executed based on titles and abstracts, with potentially pertinent articles proceeding to a comprehensive full-text review. Subsequently, two reviewers (N.N. and H.T.) independently evaluated the full-text articles for eligibility, resolving any discrepancies through discussion and consensus. Data extraction was independently performed by the two reviewers, utilizing a standardized data extraction form. The extracted information from each included study included the author ' s name, year of publication, study design, sample size, characteristics of the study population, perioperative data (such as operation time, short-term mortality, spinal cord injury, stroke, new intimal tear or dissection in the ascending aorta, and aortic rupture), as well as rates of aortic re-intervention and mortality. Any discrepancies in data extraction were resolved through discussion and consensus.

top_evidence.text: Acute type A aortic syndrome, encompassing aortic dissection and intramural hematoma (IMH), represents a critical cardiovascular emergency leading to potential life-threatening complications, including aortic rupture, cardiac tamponade, and coronary ischemia. 1 Surgical intervention stands as the gold standard for managing this condition. Retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAAD) or intramural hematoma (RTAIMH) is relatively infrequent entity characterized by the extension of the pathology from an intimal tear or disruption situated in the descending aorta. top_evidence.section: Risk Of Bias In Individual Studies
top_evidence.text: The Cochrane tool Risk of Bias Assessment Tool for Nonrandomized Studies 14 was employed to evaluate the quality of the studies in this meta-analysis. Two independent authors (N.N. and H.T.) conducted the assessment, resolving any discrepancies or con fl icts through consensus. The outcomes of the assessment were visually presented using the ' Robvis ' package in the R software. Evaluation of publication bias was conducted using funnel plots, which provide a visual representation of the distribution of study outcomes. Asymmetry in the funnel plots was assessed using the linear regression test, 12 employing modi fi ed standard error as suggested by Pustejovsky et al. 13 A signi fi cance level of p < .1 indicated the presence of publication bias.

The search strategy incorporated the following keywords: ( ' type A aortic dissection ' OR ' TAAD ' OR ' type A intramural hematoma ' OR ' type A IMH ' ) AND ( ' endovascular ' OR ' stent graft ' ) AND ( ' retrograde ' OR ' retrograde extension ' ). Two reviewers (N.N. and H.T.) independently carried out the search to identify relevant articles.
